title: Spin Addition and the Stern-Gerlach Chain
topics: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients from the ladder operators

sources.where: Ch. 9.1-9.5 (pp. 93-101): tensor products, addition of angular momenta, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
Q2 spinors, Q3 addition D_{1/2} x D_1
Q1 Stern-Gerlach with molecules, Q3 Clebsch-Gordan coefficients for l x 1/2

intro: Combine two spins and the Stern-Gerlach magnet shows the result: a molecule of two spin-$\frac12$ atoms splits into three beams, three atoms into four. The mathematics is the Clebsch-Gordan series $D_{j_1}\otimes D_{j_2}=\bigoplus_{j=|j_1-j_2|}^{j_1+j_2}D_j$, found by the highest-weight method: start with $|j_1,j_1\rangle|j_2,j_2\rangle$, apply $S_-$, and take the orthogonal combination for the next $j$. Exam standard: HS25 Q4 (spin 1) and FS24 Q3.

tutorial.title: The magnet
tutorial.html: Molecules fly from the left through the inhomogeneous field. The deflection is proportional to the total $S_z=\hbar m$, so a molecule of three spin-$\frac12$ atoms ($D_{3/2}\oplus2D_{1/2}$) lands in four spots, with intensities $1:3:3:1$ (counting the $2^3=8$ product states by their $m$).

tutorial.title: The energy ladder
tutorial.html: On the left: the three levels of $H=\frac\omega\hbar\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$ for two spin-1 particles: $\sigma=2$ (5 states, $+\hbar\omega$), $\sigma=1$ (3 states, $-\hbar\omega$), $\sigma=0$ (1 state, $-2\hbar\omega$). The bar shows $P(S_{1z}=S_{2z}=0)(t)=\frac{5+4\cos3\omega t}9$ (HS25 Q4).

tutorial.title: Consoles
tutorial.html: Library: tensor products, Clebsch-Gordan, time evolution, Stern-Gerlach. Quiz, derivation desk and fights follow the sheets. The boss gate has HS25 Q4, FS24 Q3 and the sheet 12 Clebsch-Gordan problem.

encounters.title: Tensor products and two spin-1/2: triplet, singlet, Stern-Gerlach beams

blocks.html: Two systems with Hilbert spaces $V_1,V_2$ live in $V_1\otimes V_2$ (dimension $d_1d_2$). Operators act factor-wise, $\vec S=\vec S_1\otimes1+1\otimes\vec S_2$, and $\vec S$ satisfies the same su(2) algebra. For spin-$\frac12\otimes\frac12$ the four states $|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle,\dots$ regroup:

blocks.label: script 9.3; triplet symmetric, singlet antisymmetric under exchange

blocks.html: How to find them. The state with maximal $m$ is unique, $|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle$ with $S_z=\hbar$: it is the top of a $j=1$ multiplet. Apply $S_-=S_{1-}+S_{2-}$ to get $|1,0\rangle$ and $|1,-1\rangle$. The remaining state with $m=0$ orthogonal to $|1,0\rangle$ is annihilated by $S_\pm$: it is the singlet $j=0$.

blocks.label: the coupling H = A S1.S2 splits triplet and singlet by A hbar^2

blocks.html: Stern-Gerlach with composite objects (sheet 12 Q1). The deflection measures $S_z=\hbar m$. Two spin-$\frac12$ atoms: $m=+1,0,-1$, three beams with relative intensities $1:2:1$ (the triplet's $m=0$ plus the singlet both go to $m=0$). Three spin-$\frac12$ atoms: $D_{1/2}^{\otimes3}=D_{3/2}\oplus2D_{1/2}$, four beams $m=\pm\frac32,\pm\frac12$ with intensities $1:3:3:1$. In general $N$ atoms give $N+1$ beams with binomial weights.

The beam count $N+1$ is the spin $N/2$ multiplet: the highest spin dominates the number of beams, the lower spins only add intensity at inner positions. A single beam position cannot tell triplet from singlet; a chain of magnets (rotated axes) is needed to test coherence.

Product states are not just a list of $(m_1,m_2)$: only $m=m_1+m_2$ is conserved. $|\!\uparrow\downarrow\rangle$ is a superposition of the triplet $m=0$ and the singlet. And $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$ is not $\hbar^2m_1m_2$ alone (the $S_{1+}S_{2-}$ terms).

encounters.title: The Clebsch-Gordan series and the highest-weight method (spin 1 x spin 1)

blocks.html: For two spins $j_1,j_2$ the total $\vec S=\vec S_1+\vec S_2$ has $m=m_1+m_2$, so $m_{max}=j_1+j_2$ and the allowed total spins are $\sigma=|j_1-j_2|,\dots,j_1+j_2$, each once; the dimensions add up, $(2j_1+1)(2j_2+1)=\sum_\sigma(2\sigma+1)$ (HS25 Q4(i)). For $s_1=s_2=1$:

blocks.label: HS25 Q4(ii): H = (omega/hbar) S1.S2 has energies hbar omega, -hbar omega, -2 hbar omega

blocks.html: Highest weights (HS25 Q4(iii), 5 pt). With $|m_1;m_2\rangle$ and $S_\pm|\sigma,m\rangle=\hbar\sqrt{\sigma(\sigma+1)-m(m\pm1)}\,|\sigma,m\pm1\rangle$: $\sigma=2$: $|1;1\rangle$ (unique $m=2$). $\sigma=1$: the $m=1$ states are $|1;0\rangle,|0;1\rangle$ and $|2,1\rangle\propto S_-|1;1\rangle$; the orthogonal combination is annihilated by $S_+$. $\sigma=0$: in $m=0$ (three states) require $S_+\psi=0$.

blocks.label: check S_+ |sigma,sigma> = 0; phase convention: coefficient of |sigma, m1=sigma> positive

blocks.html: Pattern. Spin-$j$ multiplets alternate in exchange symmetry: $\sigma=2,0$ symmetric under $1\leftrightarrow2$, $\sigma=1$ antisymmetric (for two equal spins $\sigma=2s$ is symmetric, then alternating). FS24 Q3(f): the state $|1,1\rangle_A|1,1\rangle_B$ has $\vec S^2=\vec S_A^2+\vec S_B^2+2S_{Az}S_{Bz}+S_{A+}S_{B-}+S_{A-}S_{B+}$, and only the diagonal terms survive: $(2+2+2)\hbar^2=6\hbar^2=2(2+1)\hbar^2$, hence $\sigma=2$. (g): total spin zero is the single state $|0,0\rangle$ above, the only state with $\sigma=0$.

The sign convention matters: the singlet sign pattern $(+,-,+)$ for $(|1;-1\rangle,|0;0\rangle,|-1;1\rangle)$ follows from the Condon-Shortley convention. Other books may differ in overall phase, never in the coefficient magnitudes $\frac1{\sqrt3}$. And do not forget the factor $\sqrt2$ in $S_-|1,1\rangle=\hbar\sqrt2\,|1,0\rangle$ for a single spin 1.

check.q: Total spins in $D_1\otimes D_1$ and degeneracies of $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2=\{+\hbar^2,-\hbar^2,-2\hbar^2\}$
The highest-weight state of the $\sigma=1$ multiplet in $D_1\otimes D_1$ is
check.explain: $S_+$ annihilates it; it is orthogonal to $|2,1\rangle$.

encounters.title: Time evolution under $H=\frac{\omega}{\hbar}\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$ and measurement probabilities (HS25 Q4 (iv)-(v))

blocks.html: Start in $|0;0\rangle=|1,0\rangle\otimes|1,0\rangle$. Expand in the eigenstates of $H$, the $|\sigma,m\rangle$, because only they evolve with a pure phase. Use the table of the previous lesson:
Energies: $E_2=+\hbar\omega$, $E_0=-2\hbar\omega$, so $|\psi(t)\rangle=\sqrt{\tfrac23}e^{-i\omega t}|2,0\rangle-\tfrac1{\sqrt3}e^{2i\omega t}|0,0\rangle$. Convert back to the product basis:

blocks.label: HS25 Q4(v); the two probabilities add to 1

blocks.html: Beat of two frequencies: $E_2-E_0=3\hbar\omega$ is the only frequency, so the whole motion has period $2\pi/3\omega$. At $t=0$ the probability to be in $|0;0\rangle$ is 1, at $3\omega t=\pi$ it drops to $\frac19$: the system oscillates between "both spins have $m=0$" and "$m_1=-m_2=\pm1$". Total $S_z=0$ is conserved throughout (the sector $m=0$ has dimension 3).

Mixed signs: the relative phase is $e^{-i(E_2-E_0)t/\hbar}=e^{-3i\omega t}$, not $e^{-i\omega t}$ alone. The normalisation check at the end: $|1-e^{3i\omega t}|^2\cdot2+|2+e^{3i\omega t}|^2=2(2-2\cos\phi)+5+4\cos\phi=9$ with $\phi=3\omega t$.

encounters.title: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients for $l\otimes\frac12$ and spin-1/2 measurements

blocks.html: The case of orbital angular momentum $l$ and spin $\frac12$ gives $D_l\otimes D_{1/2}=D_{l+1/2}\oplus D_{l-1/2}$ (dimension $(2l+1)\cdot2=(2l+2)+2l$). The Clebsch-Gordan coefficients of the upper multiplet (sheet 12 Q3(i)):

blocks.label: sheet 12 Q3 eq. (7); the lower multiplet has the same moduli with the roles exchanged and a relative minus sign

blocks.html: Derivation sketch. Highest weight: $|l+\frac12,l+\frac12\rangle=|l\rangle|\!\uparrow\rangle$. Apply $J_-=L_-+S_-$ repeatedly, with $L_-|l,m\rangle=\hbar\sqrt{(l+m)(l-m+1)}\,|l,m-1\rangle$ and $S_-|\!\uparrow\rangle=\hbar|\!\downarrow\rangle$, and compare with $J_-|j,m\rangle=\hbar\sqrt{(j+m)(j-m+1)}\,|j,m-1\rangle$. The recursion relates the coefficients at $m$ and $m-1$. Normalisation then gives the square roots above.

blocks.label: sheet 12 Q3(ii); so a spin-orbit state j=3/2, m_j=1/2 has spin up with probability 2/3

blocks.html: Spin-$\frac12$ rotations and measurements (FS24 Q3 (a)-(d)). For $|\psi\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt2}(|\!\uparrow\rangle+|\!\downarrow\rangle)$ a measurement of $S_z$ gives $\pm\frac\hbar2$ with probability $\frac12$ each, mean $0$. A rotation $O(\vec n,\theta)$ is implemented by $U=e^{-i\theta\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma/2}=\cos\frac\theta2-i\sin\frac\theta2\,\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma$. Alice rotates the particle and measures along $\vec e_z$; Bob measures the unrotated particle along $O(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z$. Because $U$ is unitary, $|\langle\!\uparrow|U\psi\rangle|^2=|\langle U^\dagger\!\uparrow|\psi\rangle|^2$ and $U^\dagger$ is the rotation by $-\theta$ of the measurement axis: identical probabilities (active = passive rotation). For $|\psi\rangle=|+x\rangle$ the mean value is $\frac\hbar2$ if the axis is $\vec e_x$.

The general rule: the probability to find spin up along $\vec e$ in a state with Bloch vector $\vec b=\langle\vec\sigma\rangle$ is $\frac12(1+\vec e\cdot\vec b)$ (sheet 11 Q2: the spinor $(\cos\frac\theta2,e^{i\phi}\sin\frac\theta2)$ has $\langle\vec\sigma\rangle=\vec e$ and $P(\uparrow_z)=\frac12(1+\cos\theta)$).

The CG recursion has a sign: the lower multiplet $|l-\frac12,m\rangle$ carries a relative minus sign. And do not swap the roles: the amplitude of spin up in $|l+\frac12,m\rangle$ has $m-\frac12$ for the orbital quantum number and the factor $(l+m+\frac12)$.

check.q: Probability of spin up in $|j=\frac32,m_j=\frac12\rangle$ for $l=1$
FS24 Q3(b): Alice's and Bob's probabilities are equal because
options: the state is an eigenstate of $S_z$
$|\langle e_z|U\psi\rangle|^2=|\langle U^\dagger e_z|\psi\rangle|^2$, and $U^\dagger$ is the inverse rotation of the measurement axis
the measurement is not affected by rotations

encounters.title: Two spin-$\frac12$: triplet and singlet from the ladder operator (script 9.3)
encounters.goal: Construct $|1,m\rangle$ and $|0,0\rangle$ in $D_{1/2}\otimes D_{1/2}$ and show $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2=\frac{\hbar^2}4,-\frac{3\hbar^2}4$.

steps.reveal: Only $|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle$ has $m=1$; $S_+|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle=0$ so it is a highest-weight state, $j=1$: $|1,1\rangle=|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle$.

$S_-|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle=\hbar(|\!\downarrow\uparrow\rangle+|\!\uparrow\downarrow\rangle)=\hbar\sqrt2\,|1,0\rangle$, so $|1,0\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt2}(|\!\uparrow\downarrow\rangle+|\!\downarrow\uparrow\rangle)$; once more: $|1,-1\rangle=|\!\downarrow\downarrow\rangle$.

The $m=0$ sector is 2-dimensional; the vector orthogonal to $|1,0\rangle$ is $\frac1{\sqrt2}(|\!\uparrow\downarrow\rangle-|\!\downarrow\uparrow\rangle)$. $S_\pm$ annihilates it, so $j=0$: $S_+(\dots)=\hbar(|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle-|\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle)/\sqrt2=0$.

$\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2=\frac12(\vec S^2-\vec S_1^2-\vec S_2^2)$ with $\vec S_i^2=\frac34\hbar^2$: triplet $\frac12(2-\frac32)\hbar^2=\frac{\hbar^2}4$, singlet $\frac12(0-\frac32)\hbar^2=-\frac{3\hbar^2}4$.

encounters.title: Spin-1 addition: highest weights and the multiplet states (HS25 Q4 (i)-(iii))
encounters.goal: For $s=1$: list allowed $S^2,S_z$, the spectrum of $\frac\omega\hbar\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$, and the highest-weight states of $D_2,D_1,D_0$.

steps.reveal: $S_z=\hbar m$, $m=m_1+m_2\in\{-2s,\dots,2s\}$; $\vec S^2=\hbar^2\sigma(\sigma+1)$ with $\sigma=0,1,\dots,2s$ (each once). Check dimension: $\sum_{\sigma=0}^{2s}(2\sigma+1)=(2s+1)^2$.
$H=\frac{\omega}{2\hbar}[\vec S^2-2\cdot2\hbar^2]$, i.e. $E_\sigma=\frac{\hbar\omega}2[\sigma(\sigma+1)-4]$: $E_2=\hbar\omega$ (5), $E_1=-\hbar\omega$ (3), $E_0=-2\hbar\omega$ (1).

$|2,2\rangle=|1;1\rangle$. For $m=1$: $S_-|1;1\rangle=\hbar\sqrt2(|0;1\rangle+|1;0\rangle)$, so $|2,1\rangle=(|1;0\rangle+|0;1\rangle)/\sqrt2$; the orthogonal combination $|1,1\rangle=(|1;0\rangle-|0;1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ is annihilated by $S_+$ ($\sqrt2-\sqrt2=0$).
Take $\psi=a|1;-1\rangle+b|0;0\rangle+c|-1;1\rangle$: $S_+\psi=\hbar\sqrt2[(a+b)|1;0\rangle+(b+c)|0;1\rangle]=0$, so $a=c=-b$ and $|0,0\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt3}(|1;-1\rangle-|0;0\rangle+|-1;1\rangle)$.

$\langle2,0|0;0\rangle=\frac2{\sqrt6}$, $\langle0,0|0;0\rangle=-\frac1{\sqrt3}$, $\langle1,0|0;0\rangle=0$: $|0;0\rangle=\frac2{\sqrt6}|2,0\rangle-\frac1{\sqrt3}|0,0\rangle$. Check: $\frac46+\frac13=1$.
$|\psi(t)\rangle=\frac2{\sqrt6}e^{-i\omega t}|2,0\rangle-\frac1{\sqrt3}e^{2i\omega t}|0,0\rangle$.

$\langle1;-1|\psi\rangle=\frac2{\sqrt6}\frac1{\sqrt6}e^{-i\omega t}-\frac1{\sqrt3}\frac1{\sqrt3}e^{2i\omega t}=\frac{e^{-i\omega t}}3(1-e^{3i\omega t})$ (same for $|-1;1\rangle$); $\langle0;0|\psi\rangle=\frac46e^{-i\omega t}+\frac13e^{2i\omega t}=\frac{e^{-i\omega t}}3(2+e^{3i\omega t})$.
$|\frac{2+e^{3i\omega t}}3|^2=\frac{4+4\cos3\omega t+1}9=\frac{5+4\cos3\omega t}9$.

encounters.title: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients $l\otimes\frac12$ (sheet 12 Q3 (i))

steps.reveal: $|l+\frac12,m\rangle=\alpha_m|m-\frac12\rangle|\!\uparrow\rangle+\beta_m|m+\frac12\rangle|\!\downarrow\rangle$ (only $m_l+m_s=m$ allowed).

$|l+\frac12,l+\frac12\rangle=|l\rangle|\!\uparrow\rangle$: $\alpha=1,\beta=0$. Apply $J_-=L_-+S_-$: $J_-(\alpha_m|m-\frac12\rangle\uparrow+\beta_m|m+\frac12\rangle\downarrow)=\hbar[\alpha_m\sqrt{(l+m-\frac12)(l-m+\frac32)}|m-\frac32\rangle\uparrow+(\alpha_m+\beta_m\sqrt{(l+m+\frac12)(l-m+\frac12)})|m-\frac12\rangle\downarrow]$.

Coefficient of $|m-\frac32\rangle\uparrow$: $\alpha_{m-1}=\alpha_m\sqrt{\frac{l+m-\frac12}{l+m+\frac12}}$ (eq. (8) of the sheet). Iterating from $\alpha_{l+1/2}=1$ gives $\alpha_m=\sqrt{\frac{l+m+\frac12}{2l+1}}$.
$\beta_m^2=1-\alpha_m^2=\frac{l-m+\frac12}{2l+1}$, with positive sign by the Condon-Shortley phase convention.

keyPoints: $m_l+m_s=m$ restricts the ansatz to two terms

encounters.title: Alice and Bob: rotating the state or the apparatus (FS24 Q3 (b)-(d))
encounters.goal: Show that the outcome probabilities of Alice (rotated particle, fixed $z$ analyser) and Bob (unrotated particle, analyser along $O(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z$) coincide, and evaluate them for $|\psi\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt2}(|\!\uparrow\rangle+|\!\downarrow\rangle)$.

steps.reveal: $P_A(\pm)=\langle\psi|U^\dagger P_\pm(\vec e_z)U|\psi\rangle$.

steps.prompt: (b) Show $U^\dagger\vec e_z\!\cdot\!\vec\sigma\,U=(R(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z)\cdot\vec\sigma$ (rotation property of the Pauli matrices).
steps.reveal: $U^\dagger\sigma_jU=R_{jk}(\vec n,\theta)^{-1}\sigma_k$-type relation: conjugating $\vec\sigma$ with $U$ rotates the vector $\vec e$ by $\mp\theta$. So $U^\dagger P_\pm(\vec e_z)U=P_\pm(R(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z)$, which is Bob's projector. Hence $P_A=P_B$ for every $\psi$.
The Bloch vector is $\hat x$. $P(\pm)=\frac12(1\pm\vec e'\cdot\hat x)$ with $\vec e'=R(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z$.

steps.prompt: (d) Choose the axis such that $\langle S\rangle=+\hbar/2$.
steps.reveal: $\langle S_{e'}\rangle=\frac\hbar2\vec e'\cdot\hat x=\frac\hbar2$ requires $\vec e'=\hat x$: the measurement axis along $x$ (e.g. $\vec n=\hat y$, rotating $z$ into $x$ by $\theta=\pm\frac\pi2$).

keyPoints: unitary rotation moves from state to apparatus
expectation $\hbar/2$ only along the state's own axis

encounters.title: Two spin-1 particles: total spin and the singlet (FS24 Q3 (e)-(g))
encounters.goal: Find the possible $(\vec S_A+\vec S_B)^2$, show $|1,1\rangle_A|1,1\rangle_B$ has $2(2+1)\hbar^2$, and find all total-spin-zero states.

steps.reveal: $\hbar^2\sigma(\sigma+1)$ with $\sigma=0,1,2$: $0,2\hbar^2,6\hbar^2$.

$S_{A+}$ annihilates $|1,1\rangle_A$ and $S_{B+}$ too; $S_{A+}S_{B-}$ gives zero (A is raised beyond the top); $S_{A-}S_{B+}$ gives zero. Remaining: $(2+2+2\cdot1\cdot1)\hbar^2=6\hbar^2=2(2+1)\hbar^2$.

steps.prompt: (g) Find all states with $\vec S^2=0$ in the $S_{Az},S_{Bz}$ basis.
steps.reveal: $S_z=0$ so $m_A=-m_B$: $\psi=a|1;-1\rangle+b|0;0\rangle+c|-1;1\rangle$. Require $S_+\psi=0$: $a=c=-b$. Unique solution $\frac1{\sqrt3}(|1;-1\rangle-|0;0\rangle+|-1;1\rangle)$ (up to a phase).
Only one $\sigma=0$ multiplet of dimension 1 appears in $9=5+3+1$: the answer must be a single state.

keyPoints: the top state is annihilated by the raising terms

encounters.title: Spectrum of $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$ for two spin-$s$ (HS25 Q4 (i)-(ii))
encounters.problem: Two spin-$s$ particles with $H=\frac\omega\hbar\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$. Find the eigenvalues and degeneracies. Source: HS25 Q4 (i)-(ii).

derivation.title: Method
derivation.html: $\vec S^2=\vec S_1^2+\vec S_2^2+2\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$, so $H$ is a function of $\vec S^2$, diagonal in $|\sigma,m\rangle$.

steps.prompt: Which values of $\sigma$ occur in $D_s\otimes D_s$ and how often?
options: $\sigma=2s$ only, since the state is symmetric

why.0: That ignores the possibility of other total spins.
why.1: $\sigma$ is an integer for two equal spins ($m=m_1+m_2$, steps of 1).
why.2: All $\sigma$ occur, alternating symmetric/antisymmetric under exchange.

steps.prompt: Type the eigenvalue of $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2/\hbar^2$ (symbols sigma, s).
steps.hint: $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2=\frac12(\vec S^2-\vec S_1^2-\vec S_2^2)$ with $\vec S_i^2=s(s+1)\hbar^2$.

steps.prompt: Check: the trace of $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$ over the whole space for $s=1$
options: $5\cdot1+3\cdot(-1)+1\cdot(-2)=0$ in units $\hbar^2$, as it must be since $\mathrm{tr}\,S_{1i}=0$

why.1: That is the dimension of the space.
why.3: The trace of a product of traceless operators on different factors vanishes.

steps.prompt: Bonus: for $s=1$ the gap $E_{\sigma=2}-E_{\sigma=0}$ in units of $\hbar\omega$.
steps.hint: $1-(-2)=3$ in units of $\hbar\omega$: the beat frequency of the HS25 evolution.

encounters.title: Time evolution and measurement probability (HS25 Q4 (iv)-(v))
encounters.problem: Two spin-1 particles with $H=\frac\omega\hbar\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$ start in $|0;0\rangle$. Find $P(S_{1z}=S_{2z}=0)$ at time $t$. Source: HS25 Q4 (iv)-(v).

derivation.title: Method
derivation.html: Expand in $|\sigma,0\rangle$ with $\sigma=2,0$, attach phases, project on $|0;0\rangle$.

why.3: The singlet contributes, the triplet is orthogonal.

steps.prompt: Type the amplitude of $|0;0\rangle$ up to the overall phase $e^{-i\omega t}$: $|\langle0;0|\psi\rangle|^2$ (symbols omega, t).
steps.hint: $|\frac{2+e^{3i\omega t}}3|^2$ with $\frac23e^{-i\omega t}+\frac13e^{2i\omega t}$ as amplitude.
Each amplitude has $|1-e^{3i\omega t}|^2/9=(2-2\cos3\omega t)/9$. The sum with $P(0;0)$ is 1.

steps.prompt: What is conserved during the motion?
options: total $S_z=0$ (the dynamics stays in the 3-dimensional $m=0$ sector) and total probability
nothing: the state is not stationary

why.2: $S_z$, $\vec S^2$ and the energy are conserved.
why.3: That is conserved, but it is trivial (equals $2\hbar^2$ always); $S_z$ is the useful one.

encounters.title: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients for $l\otimes\frac12$ (sheet 12 Q3)
encounters.problem: An electron has orbital angular momentum $l$ and spin $\frac12$. Find the probability to find spin up in $|l+\frac12,m\rangle$. Source: sheet 12 Q3.

derivation.title: Method
derivation.html: Coefficients from the lowering operator recursion; the weights are $\frac{l\pm m+1/2}{2l+1}$.

steps.prompt: How is the recursion for $\alpha_m$ obtained?
options: apply $J_+$ to the lowest state only
diagonalise $\vec L\cdot\vec S$ in the product basis
apply $J_-=L_-+S_-$ to $|l+\frac12,m\rangle$ and compare the coefficient of $|m-\frac32\rangle|\!\uparrow\rangle$ with $J_-|j,m\rangle=\hbar\sqrt{(j+m)(j-m+1)}|j,m-1\rangle$

why.0: Either direction works, but you must start from a state you know: the top state is $|l\rangle|\!\uparrow\rangle$, so lowering.
why.1: This also works but is slower and gives the eigenvalue, not the recursion.
why.2: Orthogonality gives the lower multiplet once the upper one is known.

steps.hint: Sheet 12 Q3 eq. (7): the weight of the spin-up component with $m_l=m-\frac12$.
The two weights add to one: $P_\uparrow+P_\downarrow=\frac{2l+1}{2l+1}=1$.

options: $P_\uparrow=1$: the state is $|l\rangle|\!\uparrow\rangle$ since $m_l=l$ and no spin-down component can have $m_l=l+1$

why.0: $m_l=l+1$ does not exist, so no spin-down component.

encounters.title: Spin-1 addition (HS25 Q4)
encounters.instructions: Solve on paper under the timer (2 min per point). Then enter the numbers.
statement: We consider two spin-$s$ particles with spin operators $\vec S_1,\vec S_2$. The state space of each individual particle is described by a $D_s$ representation of su(2), $D_s=\mathrm{span}\{|s,m\rangle\,|\,m=-s,\dots,s\}$, with $\hbar m$ being the eigenvalue of the $z$-component of $\vec S_i$ on the state $|s,m\rangle$. The particles are coupled by the Hamiltonian $H=\frac\omega\hbar\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$.
(i) Let $\vec S=\vec S_1+\vec S_2$ be the total spin. What are the allowed eigenvalues of $\vec S^2$ and $S_z$? [3 points]
(ii) Find the eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian and their degeneracy. [3 points] Hint: Write $\vec S_1\cdot\vec S_2$ in terms of $\vec S^2,\vec S_1^2,\vec S_2^2$.

From now on we fix the spin of the individual particle to be $s=1$. The tensor product of two spin-1 representations decomposes into $D_1\otimes D_1\cong D_0\oplus D_1\oplus D_2$. We denote the tensor product basis of $D_1\otimes D_1$ by $|m_1;m_2\rangle:=|1,m_1\rangle\otimes|1,m_2\rangle$, and the states in $D_\sigma$, $\sigma=0,1,2$, on the right-hand side by $|\sigma,m\rangle$.

(iii) Find the highest-weight states of the $D_\sigma$ representations on the right-hand side of eq. (25) in the tensor product basis $|m_1;m_2\rangle$. [5 points] Hint: On a state $|\sigma,m\rangle$ in a spin-$\sigma$ representation $D_\sigma$, the raising and lowering operators act as $S_\pm|\sigma,m\rangle=\hbar\sqrt{\sigma(\sigma+1)-m(m\pm1)}\,|\sigma,m\pm1\rangle$.

(iv) At time $t=0$, the system is in the state $|\psi(t=0)\rangle=|0;0\rangle=|1,0\rangle\otimes|1,0\rangle$. Show that the state $|\psi(t)\rangle$ at time $t$ is given by $|\psi(t)\rangle=\frac{e^{-i\omega t}}3\Big[(1-e^{3i\omega t})|1;-1\rangle+(1-e^{3i\omega t})|-1;1\rangle+(2+e^{3i\omega t})|0;0\rangle\Big]$. [7 points]
(v) At time $t$, what is the probability to measure $\langle S_{1,z}\rangle=0$ and $\langle S_{2,z}\rangle=0$? [3 points]

finalAnswers.prompt: (ii) Highest energy for $s=1$ in units of $\hbar\omega$.
(ii) Lowest energy for $s=1$ in units of $\hbar\omega$ (signed).

keyPoints: (iv) $|0;0\rangle=\frac2{\sqrt6}|2,0\rangle-\frac1{\sqrt3}|0,0\rangle$ with phases $e^{-i\omega t}$ and $e^{2i\omega t}$; project back on product states

encounters.title: Spin systems (FS24 Q3, translated)
encounters.instructions: Solve on paper under the timer (2 min per point). The statement below is a translation of the German exam text.
statement: First consider a spin-$\frac12$ particle whose spin degree of freedom is described by the state $|\psi\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt2}(|\!\uparrow\rangle+|\!\downarrow\rangle)$, where $|\!\uparrow\rangle$ is the eigenstate of $\hat S_z$ with eigenvalue $\frac\hbar2$ and $|\!\downarrow\rangle$ the eigenstate with eigenvalue $-\frac\hbar2$.
(a) What are the possible outcomes if the angular momentum of this particle is measured along the $z$-direction $\vec e_z$? With what probability do they occur and what is the expectation value? [2]

In the following $O(\vec n,\theta)\in SO(3)$ denotes a rotation by the angle $\theta$ about an axis in direction $\vec n$ ($|\vec n|^2=1$). You may use $e^{-i\frac\theta2\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma}=\cos\frac\theta2\,\mathrm{id}-i\sin\frac\theta2\,\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma$, where $\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma=n_x\sigma_x+n_y\sigma_y+n_z\sigma_z$ and $\sigma_{x,y,z}$ are the Pauli matrices. An experimenter Alice first applies the rotation $O(\vec n,\theta)$ to the particle and then measures the spin with a device along $\vec e_z$. Another experimenter Bob measures the spin of the unrotated particle directly with the device rotated in the opposite direction, i.e. along $O(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z$.
(b) Show that, independent of the initial state of the spin particle, the probabilities of the possible measurement results of Alice and Bob are equal. [6]

Now only consider Bob's experiment, in which he measures the spin of the particle described by $|\psi\rangle$ above along the axis $O(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z$. (c) With what probability do the possible results occur? [4] (d) How must the measurement axis be chosen so that the expectation value is $\frac\hbar2$? [1]

Now consider two spin-1 particles $A$ and $B$ instead of a single spin-$\frac12$ particle. (e) Which values can the total angular momentum $(\vec S_A+\vec S_B)^2$ take? [2] (f) Let the state of the total system be $|j=1,m=1\rangle_A\otimes|j=1,m=1\rangle_B$. Show that the total angular momentum $(\vec S_A+\vec S_B)^2$ has the value $2(2+1)\hbar^2$. [4] (g) Find all states for which the total angular momentum is zero. Give these states in a basis in which $\hat S_{A,z}$ and $\hat S_{B,z}$ are diagonal. [6]

finalAnswers.prompt: (e) Largest value of $(\vec S_A+\vec S_B)^2$ in units of $\hbar^2$.
(g) Number of states with total angular momentum zero.
(g) Absolute value of the coefficient of $|0;0\rangle$ in the singlet.

keyPoints: (b) Alice: $\langle\psi|U^\dagger P_\pm(\vec e_z)U|\psi\rangle$; $U^\dagger(\vec e_z\cdot\vec\sigma)U=(R(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z)\cdot\vec\sigma$: this is Bob's projector
(c) $P(\pm)=\frac12(1\pm\vec e'\cdot\hat x)$ with $\vec e'=O(\vec n,-\theta)\vec e_z$ because $|\psi\rangle=|+x\rangle$; (d) $\vec e'=\hat x$
(e) $0,2\hbar^2,6\hbar^2$; (f) $\vec S^2=\vec S_A^2+\vec S_B^2+2S_{Az}S_{Bz}+S_{A+}S_{B-}+S_{A-}S_{B+}$, the last two terms annihilate the top state, $(2+2+2)\hbar^2=6\hbar^2$

encounters.title: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and Stern-Gerlach (sheet 12 Q1 and Q3)
encounters.instructions: Sheet problems used as a boss (exam style). Solve on paper under the timer, then enter the numbers.
statement: Question 1 [Stern-Gerlach experiment]: In the Stern-Gerlach experiment, (electrically neutral) particles are shot through an inhomogeneous magnetic field. A particle is deflected up- or downwards depending on its intrinsic angular momentum, its spin. Finally, the path the particle has taken is measured by recording its incidence on a screen. Sketch the expected measurement results of Stern-Gerlach experiments carried out with molecules composed of (i) two spin-$\frac12$ atoms, (ii) three spin-$\frac12$ atoms.

Question 3 [Clebsch-Gordan coefficients] (i) Prove that the Clebsch-Gordan coefficients for the decomposition of the tensor product of spin $l$ and spin $\frac12$ to spin $l+\frac12$ are $\langle l,\tfrac12,m\mp\tfrac12,\pm\tfrac12|l,\tfrac12,l+\tfrac12,m\rangle=\sqrt{\frac{l\pm m+\frac12}{2l+1}}$. Hint: First focus on the $m_2=\frac12$ coefficients. Using one of the recursion relations from the lecture show that $\langle l,\tfrac12,m-\tfrac32,\tfrac12|l,\tfrac12,l+\tfrac12,m-1\rangle=\sqrt{\frac{l+m-\frac12}{l+m+\frac12}}\langle l,\tfrac12,m-\tfrac12,\tfrac12|l,\tfrac12,l+\tfrac12,m\rangle$. Identify the state of highest spin, then use this relation to find all the $m_2=\frac12$ coefficients. To find the $m_2=-\frac12$ coefficients, consider the other recursion relation from the lecture.

(ii) An electron in the hydrogen atom is in an orbital angular momentum state with $l=1$. Find the eigenstates of the total (orbital and spin) angular momentum $|j,j_z\rangle$ in $D_{3/2}$ in terms of those labelled by $|m,s\rangle$, where $m$ and $s$ are the $z$-components of the orbital and spin angular momentum operators, respectively.

Question 3 of sheet 11: Consider two irreducible representations $D_j$ of su(2) with spins $j=\frac12$ and $j=1$. Write their tensor product $D_{1/2}\otimes D_1$ as a sum of irreducible representations.

finalAnswers.prompt: (Q1 i) Number of beams for a molecule of 2 spin-$\frac12$ atoms.
(Q1 ii) Number of beams for 3 atoms.
Dimension check $D_{1/2}\otimes D_1$: dimension of the $D_{1/2}$ summand plus the $D_{3/2}$ summand.

keyPoints: Q1: two atoms: $D_1\oplus D_0$, beams $m=1,0,-1$ with $1:2:1$; three atoms: $D_{3/2}\oplus2D_{1/2}$, four beams $1:3:3:1$

Q3 (i): $|l+\frac12,l+\frac12\rangle=|l\rangle|\!\uparrow\rangle$; lower with $J_-=L_-+S_-$; recursion $\alpha_{m-1}=\alpha_m\sqrt{\frac{l+m-1/2}{l+m+1/2}}$; normalisation gives $\sqrt{(l\pm m+\frac12)/(2l+1)}$
